title: Year two close: the whole Torah
hook: the whole Torah, the whole prayer book, the whole year, now known from the inside
carry: the torah, the prayer, the year

segments.voice: Yesterday, Tu B'Av, borrowed white dresses and dancing in the vineyards. Your line was after mourning, love. Did you tell someone what they mean to you? Today, the last day of year two. Day six hundred ninety-six.

Five times a year, something happens in the synagogue that happens at no other moment. The reader comes to the last verse of one of the five books of the Torah. In some congregations everyone rises, and the whole room calls out together, three words: chazak, chazak, venitchazek. Be strong, be strong, and let us be strengthened. Not well done. Not congratulations. Be strong. In this year's lessons, we reached that shout four times: at the end of Exodus, of Leviticus, of Numbers, of Deuteronomy. Today we stand up one more time, at the end of the whole year.
screen: `THE LAST VERSE OF A BOOK.` → `CHAZAK, CHAZAK, VENITCHAZEK.` → `FOUR BOOKS THIS YEAR.`

segments.voice: Look back at the road. Year two began in the middle of the plagues and walked the people out of Egypt, through the sea, to Sinai, and into a tent of meeting built from everyone's gifts. Then Leviticus, the book of holiness, with its offerings and its sudden line in the old Jewish translation: "thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself." Then Numbers, forty years of wilderness, complaints and manna and a donkey that talked. Then Deuteronomy, Moses' long goodbye, ending on Mount Nebo with a land he could see and not enter, and a grave no one knows. And on Simchat Torah the scroll rolled straight back to the beginning. Then the prayer book, walked in order. Waking up and thanking God for the rooster's sense to tell day from night. The Shema, with a hand over the eyes. The Amidah, standing, feet together, three steps in. Shabbat, and the quiet personal prayers at the end. Then the year: the Days of Awe, the sukkah, the lights of winter, Purim's noise, the Passover table, forty-nine days of counting, Sinai as a wedding, Ruth choosing to stay, and this summer's walls, floor and vineyards. Put it together and you have three circles, each one turning. The Torah is read through every year and begins again the moment it ends. The prayers come back three times a day. The year comes back every year. None of them is ever finished; that's the point. So the words at the end of a book don't say you made it. They say be strong, and the plural is the key: let us be strengthened, together. A people that keeps reading the same scroll, saying the same prayers, keeping the same days, holds each other up by doing it. Tomorrow the story walks on past the Torah's last page.
screen: `EXODUS TO DEUTERONOMY.` · `THE PRAYER BOOK, PAGE BY PAGE.` · `THE YEAR, FEAST AND FAST.` · `THREE CIRCLES, NEVER FINISHED.` · then, large: `THE TORAH, THE PRAYER, THE YEAR.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: say one blessing you learned this year. Settle, and breathe. Let a few of this year's blessings pass in front of you. The morning one for the soul: my God, the soul you placed in me is pure. The one that thanks God for giving strength to the weary. Blessed is the one who spoke, and the world came to be. If you pray, choose one and say it now, in Hebrew or in English, slowly, meaning every word. If you don't pray, say quietly the one line from this year that stayed with you. Then sit with it while the bell holds the time.
Chazak. Be strong: the shout at the end of each book of the Torah, and the word for closing out the whole year of the Torah, the prayers and the calendar, each circle beginning again.
Your line: the torah, the prayer, the year. Today, tell one person something you learned this year, and let them strengthen you back. Day six hundred ninety-six.

screen: `DAY 696 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: YEAR THREE OPENS: AFTER MOSES.`

howItsDone: When the reading of each of the five books of the Torah is completed in the synagogue, the congregation, often standing, calls out "chazak, chazak, venitchazek" (be strong, be strong, and let us be strengthened), and the reader repeats it.

pairs: Moses sees the land he won't enter

myth: at the end of a book of the Torah the congregation says congratulations
they call out chazak, chazak, venitchazek: be strong, and let us be strengthened.
the Torah's reading begins again as soon as it ends
on Simchat Torah the last verse is followed straight away by the first.
year two finished four books of the Torah

fork.setup: the reader has just finished the last verse of Deuteronomy. the whole Torah is done. what does the congregation do?
options: close the scroll until next year.
begin again at Genesis straight away.
fork.reveal: on Simchat Torah the first chapter of Genesis is read right after the end of Deuteronomy. the circle never stops.

original.note: Hebrew: be strong, be strong, and let us be strengthened. said at the end of each book of the Torah.

trapdoor: what you thought: the end of a year of lessons.
what it means: the whole Torah, the prayer book and the Jewish year, walked from the inside, and every circle starts again.
what a scholar hears: some hear in chazak Moses' charge to Joshua, be strong and of good courage, said as the reading moves on past one book into the next.

notes: Chazak custom: Ashkenazi congregations call 'chazak, chazak, venitchazek' at the end of each book; Sephardi custom differs (often 'chazak u'baruch' to the reader). The script says 'in many congregations'; a Keeper may want to name the variation.
Standing for the end of a book is a widespread but not universal custom.
The link of chazak to Moses' charge to Joshua (Deut 31:7, Joshua 1) is a common explanation; verify phrasing in the trapdoor.
Year-two look-back summarizes Blocks A–F of y2.md; check that the named items (talking donkey, rooster blessing, three steps, Sinai as a wedding, Ruth) match earlier days.
Blessings in the practice are described in English paraphrase, not quoted from a translation; no new prayer is written.
'Five times a year': once per book in the annual cycle; Simchat Torah completes Deuteronomy.

Editor review (2026-10-01): "many congregations" softened to "some"; "that shout came four times" made about this year's lessons, not the listener's synagogue; fixed the garbled line "the words at the end of a book aren't you made it"; trapdoor's chazak-Joshua link marked as an interpretation ("some hear").
